bibl.title: Perceived variety, psychological needs satisfaction and exercise-related well-being

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: prediction
span.quote: Perceived variety in exercise was found to prospectively predict unique variance in indices of exercise-related well-being, in addition to that explained by psychological needs for competence, relatedness, and autonomy.

span.label: perceived variety in exercise and exercise-related well-being
span.quote: The primary purpose of this study was to examine whether perceived variety in exercise predicts unique variance in exercise-related well-being over time, in addition to that explained by the three basic psychological needs embedded within BPNT (i.e., competence, relatedness, and autonomy).

span.label: prospective-observational-survey
span.quote: Using a prospective observational design, consenting participants completed the same online questionnaire (which included a battery of instruments and took approximately 15 minutes) at two time points, six weeks apart.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the instrument is built in three declared steps - item development, focus groups, and expert review - used to develop AND refine the items rather than only to produce them
span.quote: We used a three-step process including item development, focus groups, and expert review to develop and refine items that assess perceptions of experiencing variety in exercise.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the focus groups use a modified retrospective think-aloud protocol, whose stated purpose is to understand how members of the target population INTERPRET and respond to the items
span.quote: A modified ‘retrospective think-aloud’ protocol (Oremus, Cosby, & Wolfson, 2005; Willis, 2005) was used in the focus groups in order to better understand how members of the target population interpret and respond to items.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the refinement has a STOPPING RULE rather than a fixed number of rounds: transcripts are coded by constant comparison for places where a participant raised concern with an item, and the cycle repeats after each group until no new suggestions emerge
span.quote: We used a constant comparison approach (Strauss & Corbin, 1998) to identify and code sentences and phrases in which participants raised concern with one or more items. The analysis focused on problematic and alternative interpretations of items. This iterative process was repeated following each focus group and revisions were made to the questionnaire until no new suggestions emerged.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: latent variable regression is chosen over multiple regression for a stated reason: multiple regression assumes the variables are measured without error, and the authors say that assumption would produce biased estimates here
span.quote: For this study, LVR analysis is preferable to techniques such as multiple regression analysis, because it is not based on the assumption that measurement of the variables is error-free and therefore we avoid potentially producing biased estimates

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the chi-square test is deliberately not relied on alone, because a non-significant chi-square is called unrealistic, so supplementary indices are examined too - with separate numerical bands DESIGNATED for good fit and for excellent fit
span.quote: The χ2 test was considered for the model, however a non-significant χ2 statistic is considered unrealistic (Barrett, 2007) so supplementary fit indices were also examined. To assess the model we compared the χ2 goodness of fit indices, comparative fit indices (CFI), Tucker-Lewis indices (TLI), and the root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA) for each model. Criterion for evaluating good model-data fit were designated as CFI and TLI values > .90, and RMSEA values < .08, and excellent fit for CFI and TLI values > .95, and RMSEA values < .06

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: discriminant validity is given a numerical criterion rather than an impression: the average variance extracted for a construct must exceed the SQUARED CORRELATION between it and any other construct, alongside stated floors for loadings and composite reliability
span.quote: According to Hair, Black, Babin, and Anderson (2009) the factor loadings should be .50 or greater, the CR values should be .70 or greater, and Fornell and Larcker (1981) recommend that AVE values should exceed the squared correlation between that and any other construct.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: relative importance among predictors is decided by an index with a cut-off DERIVED from the number of predictors rather than chosen - one over twice the predictor count, which in this analysis makes the threshold 0.13
span.quote: An index score less than 1/ (2 × number of predictor variables) classifies the variable as relatively unimportant (Thomas, 1992). The cut-off value was 0.13 (i.e., 13%) for the LVR analyses, indicating that any RPI value below this is considered unimportant (Thomas, 1992).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE KEY TEST IS BUILT AS A COMPETING MODEL, NOT A CORRELATION: a three-factor structure is fitted specifically to see whether the new construct is empirically synonymous with one of the three established needs, and the authors state in advance what result would count against their own claim
span.quote: A three factor model was examined to test the extent to which variety might be empirically synonymous (i.e., lacks discriminant validity) with one or more of the three psychological needs conceptualized within BPNT. Should empirical evidence suggest that perceived variety in exercise is highly correlated with, and undistinguishable from, one or more of the three psychological needs, then this would challenge the contention that perceived variety is a distinct construct

span.label: The design is non-experimental, so no causal inference is licensed; experiments are needed.
span.note: what this limits: any causal reading: EXPERIMENTAL DESIGNS WILL BE NECESSARY IN FUTURE RESEARCH TO EXAMINE THE EXTENT TO WHICH CHANGES ... RELATE[] TO CHANGES IN EXERCIS[e]
span.quote: Experimental designs will be necessary in future research to examine the extent to which changes (and frustration) in the experience of variety in exercise relates to changes in exercise-related well-being (and ill-being) outcomes.

span.label: Variety was assessed only at the contextual level.
span.note: what this limits: the level at which the finding holds: assessments of perceived variety were operationalised AT THE CONTEXTUAL LEVEL only
span.quote: A second limitation of the study corresponds to the contextual level through which we operationalized assessments of perceived variety.

span.label: The results say nothing about acute/episodic effects of perceived variety or about global life-level effects.
span.note: what this limits: acute and global claims: THE RESULTS OF THE STUDY DO NOT PROV[ide evidence] about episodic effects or life-level outcomes
span.quote: Specifically, although we would certainly expect that experiencing variety in the context of exercise would be related to various adaptive outcomes, the results of the study do not provide insight into the acute effects of perceived variety on the immediate/episodic experience of well-being, or any global effects of experiencing variety within life in general.

span.label: The factor structure was verified on the same sample used to derive it, only at a different time point.
span.note: what this limits: the factor structure itself: THE USE OF THE SAME SAMPLE TO VERIFY THE FACTOR STRUCTURE (ALBEIT AT DIFFERENT TIME POINTS) AND RESULTS SHOULD BE INTERPRETED WITH CAUTION
span.quote: A final limitation corresponds to the use of the same sample to verify the factor structure (albeit at different time points) and results should be interpreted with caution.

span.label: Whether the new construct is distinct from the three established needs, or subsumed by them, was an open question this study set out to examine rather than assume.
span.note: what this limits: perceived variety as an established separate need: the paper examines whether it is distinct from or subsumed by competence, relatedness and autonomy
span.quote: We also examined the extent to which variance in perceived variety is empirically distinct from (or subsumed by), competence, relatedness, and autonomy in the context of exercise.

span.label: The construct it is measured alongside has been operationalised inconsistently in the literature, sometimes as a single latent variable.
span.note: what this limits: comparisons with other needs-satisfaction studies: the paper notes the construct has at times been operationalised as a single latent variable, and tests a one-factor model for that reason
span.quote: Psychological needs satisfaction has at times been operationalized as a single latent variable (e.g., Johnson & Finney, 2010)

span.label: perceived variety
span.quote: We also examined the extent to which variance in perceived variety is empirically distinct from (or subsumed by), competence, relatedness, and autonomy in the context of exercise.

span.label: psychological needs satisfaction
span.quote: Psychological needs satisfaction has at times been operationalized as a single latent variable (e.g., Johnson & Finney, 2010)

span.label: variety - the general stipulated definition: the pursuit and experience of diverse activities, behaviours and opportunities in one's social milieu
span.quote: We defined variety as the pursuit and experience of diverse activities, behaviors, and opportunities in one’s social milieu

span.label: variety - the narrower sense used in this study, which explicitly admits simple, mundane and conventional experiences and so is not sensation-seeking
span.quote: and/or alternating familiar experiences, which could also be simple, mundane, and conventional.

span.label: replicates → Sheldon and Lyubomirsky (2012), conclusion that perceptions of variety directly predict well-being
span.quote: The current findings are consistent with Sheldon and Lyubomirsky’s (2012) conclusions that perceptions of variety directly predict indices of well-being.

span.label: extends → Sheldon and Lyubomirsky (2012)
span.quote: We extended their work by demonstrating that in the context of exercise, perceived variety complements the three psychological needs incorporated within BPNT in the prediction of exercise-related well-being.

span.label: builds-on → Kahn and Ratner (2005) and Sheldon and Lyubomirsky (2012), definition of variety
span.quote: We defined variety as the pursuit and experience of diverse activities, behaviors, and opportunities in one’s social milieu (cf. Kahn & Ratner, 2005; Sheldon & Lyubomirsky, 2012).

span.label: perceived variety —distinct-from→ psychological needs satisfaction
span.quote: We also examined the extent to which variance in perceived variety is empirically distinct from (or subsumed by), competence, relatedness, and autonomy in the context of exercise.
